parsed.why: Strongest local protections: 1993 nondiscrimination and hate-crime coverage, shield law reaching travelling families, open ID rules, top protective tier. Parent passport/entry regime and dated 2012 birth-sex custody keep it below low-risk.

Most-protective tier state: nondiscrimination since 2001, hate-crime coverage, panic-defence repeal, X markers, listed shield laws. Shield scope for visitors unresolved and parent border/document regime still binds; marginally below dossier 1.

Sanctuary care shield, identity-based prison housing and top protective laws, but documented hostility: highest raw incident count, rising city hate-crime reports, governor platforming anti-trans figures. Protective law plus active public hostility sits a step below dossiers 1-2.

Adds its own hostile layer under parent 0.35: birth-sex restroom ban with police ID checks, binary definition act barring marker changes, no nondiscrimination, hate-crime law excluding gender identity, surgery-denial affirmed, top Do-Not-Travel tier.

Facility ban with private cause of action, school birth-sex rule, no nondiscrimination or state hate-crime law, Negative-band rating, worst-legislation list. Slightly above 4: no documented police enforcement and no Do-Not-Travel placement, but tier-1 exposure persists.
